q: How do we account for product samples sent to buyers and trade fairs?
title: Product samples in Scope 3
short: Samples you make are already in your Scope 1 and 2 through plant energy, and their materials are in Category 1 with your other purchases. Courier and air freight you pay to send them is Category 4. Count sample freight separately: air couriers to overseas buyers can be noticeable.

ul: Sampling done in your own unit uses your fuel and electricity: already in Scope 1 and 2.
Fabric, yarn and trims for samples are part of your purchases: already in Category 1.
Samples bought from another maker are purchased goods: Category 1.
International courier invoices show weight and destination: use them for a distance and weight estimate, or the carrier's emission statement if it provides one.
Air freight per kg is many times road or sea per kg.

p: Digital samples, consolidating samples into fewer shipments and using a local sampling office cut courier weight. Record the change in kilograms sent.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase and service invoices; it uses quantities where the invoice shows them and otherwise gives a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based with wider uncertainty.
